topic.name: The Dimension of the Null Space of a Matrix

question.text: Let $R$ be a $8 \times 12$ matrix that has $8$ pivot columns. What is the dimension of the null space of $R?$
question.explanation:
We know that $\textrm{dim(Null}(R))$ is the number of non-pivot columns in $R.$

Since $R$ has $12$ columns and $8$ of them are pivots, then the number of non-pivot columns in $R$ is \[ 12-8=4. \]

Therefore, $\textrm{dim(Null}(R))=4.$

example.title: Determining the Dimension of the Null Space of a Matrix Given the Number of Non-Pivot Columns

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true?

  1. If $A=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ then $\textrm{dim(Null}(A))=0.$
  2. If $B=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ then $\textrm{dim(Null}(B))=2.$
  3. If $C=\begin{bmatrix} 5 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ then $\textrm{dim(Null}(C))=1.$
question.explanation:
The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix.

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

  • Statement I is true. The matrix $A$ has $2$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. So, \[ \textrm{dim(Null}(A))=0. \]

  • Statement II is false. The matrix $B$ has $2$ pivot column and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $3$rd column). So, \[ \textrm{dim(Null}(B))=1. \]

  • Statement III is true. The matrix $C$ has $2$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $2$nd column). So, \[ \textrm{dim(Null}(C))=1. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

example.title: Identifying the Dimension of the Null Space of Matrices Using Inspection

question.explanation:
To find $\textrm{dim}(\textrm{Null}(A))$, we reduce $A$ to row echelon form, as follows:

\begin{align*} A &= \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 & 1 & 2\\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 8 & 0 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} & R_3 &:= R_3 + (-2)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 & 1 & 2\\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} & R_3 &:= R_3 + R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 & 1 & 2\\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} & R_4 &:= R_4 + \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 & 1 & 2\\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $4$th column).

Therefore,

\[ \textrm{dim}(\textrm{Null}(A)) = 1. \]

example.title: Finding the Nullity of a Matrix Using Row Reduction

question.explanation:
To find $\textrm{dim}(\textrm{Null}(G))$, we reduce $G$ to row echelon form, as follows:

\begin{align*} G &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ -2 & 3 & -6 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 & 1 \\ -6 & -15 & -12 & -16 \end{bmatrix} & R_2 &:= R_2 + R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 & 1 \\ -6 & -15 & -12 & -16 \end{bmatrix} & R_4 &:= R_4 + 3R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7 \end{bmatrix} & R_3 &:= R_3 + \dfrac{1}{4}R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & \dfrac{9}{2} & \dfrac{11}{4} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

The reduced matrix has $4$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns.

Therefore,

\[ \textrm{dim}(\textrm{Null}(G)) = 0. \]

example.title: Finding the Nullity of a Matrix Using Row Reduction

question.text:
Consider the matrices given below. Find $\textrm{dim(Null}(A)) + \textrm{dim(Null}(B)) + \textrm{dim(Null}(C)).$

\[ A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad C = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix.

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

  • The matrix $A$ has $1$ pivot column and $2$ non-pivot columns (namely, the $2$nd and $3$rd columns). So, \[ \textrm{dim(Null}(A))=2. \]

  • The matrix $B$ has $3$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $4$th column). So, \[ \textrm{dim(Null}(B))=1. \]

  • The matrix $C$ has $3$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $3$rd column). So, \[ \textrm{dim(Null}(C))=1. \]

Therefore, \[ \textrm{dim(Null}(A)) + \textrm{dim(Null}(B)) + \textrm{dim(Null}(C)) = 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. \]
